titre: The First Short-Story Feuilleton Did Not Appear in Girardin's La Presse
accroche: On July 1, 1836, Girardin launches La Presse at 40 francs; the same day, his competitor's Le Siècle publishes the first short-story feuilleton, a brief work of fiction.
contenu_vulgarise:
## Two Newspapers, One Day

On July 1, 1836, Émile de Girardin launched *La Presse* (*The Press*) and Armand Dutacq launched *Le Siècle* (*The Century*). Both rested on the same strategy: the “40-franc” press, which cut the subscription price in half thanks to advertising revenue and considerably increased circulation. The word “feuilleton” already existed: since January 28, 1800, the *Journal des débats* (*Journal of Debates*) had published a “feuilleton,” first devoted mainly to theater listings and announcements, then to criticism. With the cheap press, this bottom-of-the-page space opened up to fiction.

## What the Dates Show

According to the historian Chantal Massol, the driving role in the rise of these “fiction feuilletons” does not belong to *La Presse*, despite Girardin's decisive part in promoting the new journalism, but to *Le Siècle*, a newspaper of the dynastic left, opposed to the government, which drew its readership, more than *La Presse* did, from the middle classes. On July 1, 1836, it is in *Le Siècle* that the first short-story feuilleton (“feuilleton-nouvelle”) appears: *La Nuit du Candilejo* (*The Night of Candilejo*), by Louis Viardot, published in a single installment. *La Presse*, for its part, took in serialized fiction only later: from July 17 according to Massol, with an unfinished historical novel by Dumas in ten installments, then on August 30 with a short story by Frédéric Soulié. (Wikipedia dates to July 15 the appearance of Dumas's *La Comtesse de Salisbury* (*The Countess of Salisbury*) in *La Presse*: the discrepancy does not change the order of events.) The number of works of fiction published by *La Presse* remained, that year and the following ones, well below that of *Le Siècle*, which quickly obtained three times as many subscribers as its competitor: 30,000 against 10,000 after a few months, a figure that Massol takes from Lise Queffélec.

## What Girardin Imposed

Girardin therefore did not publish the first short-story feuilleton: he above all made an economic model (low-priced press, advertising revenue, novels to build reader loyalty) visible enough for other newspapers to follow it. His *Presse* then published Balzac's *La Vieille Fille* (*The Old Maid*) (from October 23 to November 30, 1836), then, starting in December 1840, Eugène Sue's *Mathilde*, paid by the page for his first success. With *Les Mystères de Paris* (*The Mysteries of Paris*) (1842-1843), Sue achieved the first true triumph of the novel feuilleton, which took hold from 1841 and gradually supplanted short fiction. But on July 1, 1836, the day both dailies launched, priority in serialized fiction belongs to the competitor who is cited less often.

repere.texte: On July 1, 1836, Armand Dutacq's Le Siècle publishes Louis Viardot's La Nuit du Candilejo, the first short-story feuilleton, in a single installment; Émile de Girardin's La Presse, launched the same day, takes in serialized fiction only on July 17.
repere.source: Chantal Massol, “Le feuilleton-nouvelle (1836-1841)” (“The Short-Story Feuilleton, 1836-1841”), UGA Éditions, 2023

carte.punch: The first short-story feuilleton did not appear at Girardin's paper, but at his competitor's.
carte.idee: On July 1, 1836, Girardin launches La Presse the same day that Armand Dutacq launches Le Siècle. Yet it is Le Siècle that publishes, that day, the first short-story feuilleton: La Presse takes in serialized fiction only on July 17, more than two weeks later.

quiz.question: Who publishes the first short-story feuilleton on July 1, 1836, rather than Émile de Girardin's La Presse, launched the same day?
choix: The Journal des débats, which had created the “feuilleton” section as early as 1800
La Presse itself, with an unfinished historical novel by Alexandre Dumas
La Patrie, with Ponson du Terrail's L'Héritage mystérieux
Le Siècle, Armand Dutacq's newspaper, with Louis Viardot's La Nuit du Candilejo
quiz.explication: La Presse takes in serialized fiction only on July 17 according to Massol; it is Le Siècle that publishes the first short-story feuilleton, on the very day both newspapers launch.

quiz_supplementaire.question: According to the historian Chantal Massol, what distinguishes Le Siècle from La Presse in the first years of the fiction feuilleton?
choix: A readership drawn more from the middle classes and quickly three times as many subscribers
A line favorable to the government, which earns it most of its subscribers
A launch several months earlier than that of La Presse
A smaller number of works of fiction published than La Presse
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Le Siècle, a newspaper of the dynastic left opposed to the government, draws its readership more than La Presse does from the middle classes and quickly obtains three times as many subscribers; it launches the same day as La Presse and publishes far more fiction.

quiz_supplementaire.question: If the driving role in serialized fiction belongs to Le Siècle, what is Girardin really credited with?
choix: The invention of the word “feuilleton,” which he is the first to use in 1836
The creation of the status of salaried author, invented to pay Eugène Sue
An economic model (a 40-franc press financed by advertising) that other newspapers then follow
The first short-story feuilleton, La Nuit du Candilejo, published in La Presse on July 1, 1836
quiz_supplementaire.explication: Girardin popularizes the 40-franc press financed by advertising, which other newspapers follow; the word “feuilleton” dates from 1800, Sue is paid by the page, and La Nuit du Candilejo appears in Le Siècle.
